source_request: Harden the WarpOS update pipeline against the systemic Windows brittleness exposed in the 2026-05-13 multi-hour update session. Implement the architectural fixes prescribed by the GPT-5.5 review at .warpos/codex-consult-prompt.md: (1) centralize hash logic into scripts/warpos/lib/content-hash.js, (2) un-truncate capsule sha256 (full 64-char) with back-compat for 0.6.x prefixes, (3) consolidate the 4 narrow preflight overrides + --skip-preflight into a single --operator-override <gate-name> --override-reason <text> with audit logging, (4) separate the release pipeline from the apply pipeline (shared code limited to manifest schema + content-hash), (5) stop shipping migrations/ as installed assets, (6) introduce framework_template → project_owned ownership transition so consumer content in former-template paths survives framework version changes.
interpreted_intent: User wants the architectural backlog GPT-5.5 prescribed turned into a real sprint plan. The mid-session fixes that shipped in 0.6.1 (LF tolerance in classifier + manifest-honesty, hash-truncation tolerance) are insufficient as a permanent solution — they're patches over the symptom layer. The structural causes (untruncated hashes, gate rigidity, migrations-as-assets, framework-template ownership ambiguity, release/apply coupling) remain. This sprint addresses them so future consumer updates don't reproduce the May 13 nightmare.
user_or_business_outcome: Operator can run /warp:update on any clean Windows consumer (autocrlf=true) and have it complete in under 60 seconds with zero MERGE_CONFLICT or DELETE_CONFLICT false positives. Operator confidence in the update tooling restored. Future framework releases ship and apply without the multi-hour debugging cycle that motivated this sprint.

current_behavior.notes: Update pipeline assumes byte-perfect equality across LF/CRLF boundaries. On Windows (autocrlf=true), every text framework file produces a MERGE_CONFLICT false positive on first /warp:update. Capsule manifest's sha256 is truncated to 12 chars (generate-framework-manifest.js:121), propagated into framework-installed.json via update.js:490, then compared with === against full 64-char local sha — never matches. Preflight has 10 gates with override flags for only 4 (install-baseline, capsule-resolvable, version-quorum, staleness); the other 6 (manifest-honesty, path-resolution, structure-parity, applied-migrations, migration-presence, tracked-transients) have no override path. --skip-preflight exists but the code itself flags it 'NOT recommended'. Migrations ship as framework assets in capsule's framework-manifest.json#assets[]; apply copies them; applied-migrations gate flags them stale; operator deletes; next apply re-copies — infinite loop unless deleted post-apply. Consumer content placed in former-framework-template paths (e.g. _requirements/00-canonical/*.md, observed in jobhunter-app's Jobzooka project brief) gets classified DELETE_CONFLICT on framework version changes that drop the templates.

desired_behavior: Single /warp:update --source <canonical> --target <consumer> --to <version> --apply completes cleanly on Windows with 540+ Class A items and 0 Class C, no manual file shuffling, no --skip-preflight escape. Preflight overrides require explicit gate name + reason and emit audit log. Migrations stay in canonical only. Project content in framework template dirs survives version transitions. Capsule manifests are unambiguous about file content (full 64-char hash, single canonical comparison).

high_level_story_candidates: As an operator on Windows, I can run /warp:update against any new release and have it complete cleanly without surfacing line-ending bugs.
As a framework maintainer, I can audit every operator override after the fact and see which gate, why, when, by whom.
As a consumer project owner, I can put real content in former-framework-template paths without losing it when the framework restructures.
As the release author, I can produce a capsule whose framework-manifest.json is unambiguous about every file's content (single canonical hash form).
As a downstream consumer, I can update from a 0.6.x capsule even after the framework moves to 0.7.0 hash format (read back-compat).
